names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 9 aprilie, «Sfântul Cuvios Vadim, arhimandritul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Βάδιμος οσιομάρτυρας και οι επτά Μαθητές του», with the rank word and the clause naming his disciples left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 9 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Преп. муч. Вадим.“, with Преп. муч. left off — the rank words this source uses for a venerable-martyr, which this folder already carries in `types`. The heading leaves no epithet and names neither the monastery nor the country, so the bare forename is what the source gives; it folds with nothing, no other folder holding a Serbian Вадим.

Read out of the title on the name link behind his line for 9 апреля ст. ст., name page 330, «Вадим Персидский, архимандрит, сщмч.», with the office word and the rank abbreviation left off. The day’s own line gives the forename alone in the genitive, «Вадима», with «архимандрита» beside it. The bare «Вадим» is the `sr` form this same folder already holds off the Ohrid Prologue, so the epithet the name page prints is what is stored, and it keeps the two forms distinct as well as faithful. `.tmp/foldchk.py` and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` were both run before this draft: no folder holds this form, and it adds a key no other folder holds.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 апреля ст. ст. — «Прмч. Вадима архимандрита и 7 учеников его (376).»

feast.note: The day page and the life page agree on 9 aprilie as the commemoration, but the life itself says he was killed «în 8 Aprilie»; the day is the calendar's, the 8th is the life's date of death.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 9 aprilie — «Sfântul Cuvios Vadim, arhimandritul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Βάδιμος οσιομάρτυρας και οι επτά Μαθητές του»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 9 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and heads him «(; - 376)». The line names his seven disciples only as his seven, and the page names not one of them, so no folder was drafted for them; the companionship stands in his own life. It names their executioner, Nirsan, who had denied Christ before the torments and was afterwards killed with a knife by an idolater who grew angry with him.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.04.2026 (9. април ст. ст.) — „Преп. муч. Вадим.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek both keep him on. The man is the same beyond doubt: the abbot famed for piety, thrown into prison with seven disciples under the Persian king Shapur; the prince Nirsan imprisoned with them, who lost his faith and promised to worship the sun; the offer of Vadim's monastery if he would do the beheading with his own hand; the trembling arm and the many blows; and the year. The **376 agrees exactly** with the 376 this folder holds off saint.gr's heading, so **no date was touched**. **A second witness on how Nirsan died, and it settles nothing but moves the balance.** This entry says he soon fell into despair and **ran himself through with the sword**, receiving from his own hand the punishment for the murder of a righteous man; doxologia says he «came to a bad end and died by the sword, his own killer in despair», which reads the same way; saint.gr says an idolater grew angry with him one day and killed him with a knife. Two readings to one for the suicide, nothing changed, and the disagreement is now recorded in the life from both sides. New besides: that it was Nirsan's **promise to worship the sun** that pleased Shapur and drew the offer, where doxologia has him simply offer to do whatever was commanded; and that what stayed his hand was **the dignified face of the saint**. **The Prologue's rank word is игуман, abbot, and no type was added for it**: `BRIEF-SERBIAN.md` §5 maps игуман to `abbot`, but this folder already records «Archimandrite» in `office` from doxologia, and adding `abbot` to `types` would change what `lib/honorific.js` prints over a martyr whose other two sources call him a priest and an archimandrite — a visible change for no new fact. The rank word is recorded here instead. **The seven disciples are named by no source read for this folder**, this one included, and no folder was made for any of them. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion, and this folder has no hymn from any source.

death.note: saint.gr heads him «Αγιος Βαδιμος Οσιομαρτυρας Και Οι Επτα Μαθητες Του (; - 376)». The page’s prose gives no year of its own, setting him only in the reign of «Σαπώρ ο Β' (325 - 379 μ.Χ.)», within which the heading’s year falls. **days.pravoslavie.ru is a second witness for 376 and prints it twice**: on its day line for 9 апреля ст. ст., «Прмч. Вадима архимандрита и 7 учеников его (376).», and at the end of its life page, where the executioner at last struck the head off «(+ 376)». That page dates Shapur’s reign «(310 - 381)» instead, and 376 falls inside that too, so the two reign readings do not disturb the year. The Ohrid Prologue also closes on 376.
